title: Economic Growth Internship at Greater Washington Partnership 2026 in Washington, DC (Paid Opportunity – $20 Per Hour)
summary: The Greater Washington Partnership (GWP) is inviting applications for its Fall 2026 Economic Growth Internship , offering an exciting opportunity for students and recent graduates who are passionate about economic development, entrepreneurship, regional growth, innovation, and public-private collaboration. This paid internship places successful applicants at the center of one of the United States most influential regional economic organizations, where they will contribute to initiatives that shape the future of the Greater Washington metropolitan region. The internship provides participants with meaningful professional experience by allowing them to work alongside policy experts, business leaders, government officials, nonprofit organizations, and economic development professionals. Interns will contribute to research, stakeholder engagement, event coordination, and strategic initiatives designed to strengthen economic competitiveness across Maryland, Virginia, and Washington, DC. If you are looking for an internship that combines research, policy, business strategy, entrepreneurship, and regional development, this opportunity offers an outstanding platform to gain practical experience while building valuable professional networks. About Greater Washington Partnership The Greater Washington Partnership is a unique nonprofit alliance that brings together many of the most influential employers throughout the Greater Washington region, spanning Maryland, Virginia, and the District of Columbia. Unlike traditional nonprofit organizations, the Partnership serves as a bridge between the public, private, and nonprofit sectors. It convenes leaders from business, government, education, and community organizations to solve regional challenges and promote sustainable economic growth. Its mission focuses on addressing critical issues including: Skills and workforce development Talent attraction and retention Regional transportation and mobility Infrastructure development Inclusive economic growth Entrepreneurship Innovation Business competitiveness The Partnership envisions transforming the corridor stretching from Baltimore to Richmond into one of the world s most competitive, prosperous, and attractive places to live, work, invest, and build businesses. About the Economic Growth Internship The Fall 2026 Economic Growth Internship is designed for individuals interested in understanding how regional economies grow and how cross-sector partnerships influence public policy, innovation, entrepreneurship, and economic opportunity. The internship supports implementation of the organization s Region Rising Report , a strategic roadmap released in 2026 that outlines priorities for creating a stronger and more resilient regional economy. Interns will become active contributors to projects that advance these priorities through research, stakeholder engagement, innovation programming, and policy support. Rather than observing from the sidelines, interns become part of the Economic Growth team, contributing ideas and supporting projects that directly influence regional development initiatives. Internship Responsibilities Selected interns will participate in a broad range of professional activities, including: 1. Research and Policy Analysis Interns will conduct detailed research across several important policy and economic topics, including: Regional economic development Entrepreneurship Procurement Affordable housing Financial inclusion Innovation ecosystems Business competitiveness They will also analyze findings and prepare concise reports that help guide strategic decision-making. 2. Stakeholder Engagement Interns will help coordinate collaboration among numerous stakeholders by: Scheduling meetings Preparing meeting agendas Developing briefing materials Recording meeting notes Tracking follow-up actions Supporting ongoing communication This exposure provides firsthand experience in managing relationships across multiple sectors. 3. Supporting the Region Rising Initiative The internship directly supports implementation of the Partnership s Region Rising Report . Interns will assist with: Research supporting report initiatives Monitoring progress Gathering economic insights Supporting strategic projects Coordinating implementation activities 4. Entrepreneurship and Innovation Programs Interns will contribute to programs that promote innovation throughout the region. This includes supporting the Partnership s Next Level Accelerator , which works with entrepreneurs and startup ecosystems. Responsibilities may include: Assisting with entrepreneur engagement Supporting accelerator programming Researching innovation trends Helping organize entrepreneurship initiatives 5. Event Planning and Coordination Interns will work with several internal departments to support events and public engagement. Tasks may include: Coordinating logistics Preparing event materials Communicating with speakers Supporting registrations Assisting during live events Helping with post-event follow-up 6. Cross-Functional Collaboration Interns will collaborate with various organizational teams including: Marketing Communications Public Policy Business Development Events Economic Growth This interdisciplinary exposure allows interns to understand how nonprofit organizations coordinate large-scale regional initiatives. 7. Strategic Thinking Rather than simply completing administrative tasks, interns are encouraged to contribute ideas and serve as thought partners on improving the Partnership s economic growth initiatives. Internship Benefits Participants can expect numerous professional benefits, including: Paid internship at $20 per hour Practical experience in economic development Exposure to regional policy development Networking with business and government leaders Experience working within a leading nonprofit organization Professional mentorship Research and analytical experience Event management experience Collaboration across multiple sectors Enhanced communication and leadership skills Strong resume-building experience Exposure to entrepreneurship ecosystems Internship Schedule The internship is expected to begin: End of August 2026 Early September 2026 Work schedule: Tuesdays Wednesdays Thursdays Expected weekly commitment: 25–29 hours per week Internship Location Washington, DC The Partnership s office is: Located south of Dupont Circle Accessible by Metro Positioned within one of the nation s leading policy and business hubs Compensation Selected interns will receive: $20 per hour This makes the internship both professionally rewarding and financially beneficial for students and recent graduates. Required Qualifications Applicants should meet the following requirements: Currently enrolled as a junior or senior undergraduate student OR enrolled in a postgraduate program OR be a recent graduate Strong written communication skills Strong verbal communication skills Excellent presentation skills Proficiency with Microsoft PowerPoint Experience using Microsoft Excel Familiarity with Microsoft Word Ability to thrive in a fast-paced work environment Strong organizational abilities Ability to manage multiple assignments simultaneously Comfortable working with evolving priorities Team-oriented mindset Curiosity about regional economic growth Interest in cross-sector collaboration Preferred Qualifications Although not mandatory, the following qualifications will strengthen an application: Previous internship experience Work-based learning experience Interest in entrepreneurship Interest in procurement Interest in affordable housing Interest in financial inclusion Data analysis experience Data visualization skills Creative problem-solving ability Resourcefulness Familiarity with the Baltimore-to-Richmond region Event coordination experience Why This Internship Stands Out Many internships focus narrowly on administrative work. This internship offers significantly broader exposure by allowing participants to contribute to: Public-private partnerships Economic research Entrepreneurship ecosystems Regional competitiveness Policy development Innovation strategy Stakeholder engagement Economic inclusion Participants gain insight into how large-scale economic initiatives are developed and implemented while building relationships with influential leaders from multiple sectors. Who Should Apply? This opportunity is ideal for students and recent graduates interested in careers involving: Economic development Public policy Urban planning Government relations Public administration Business strategy Entrepreneurship Economic research Consulting Nonprofit leadership Regional planning Innovation management APPLY HERE Important Information Organization: Greater Washington Partnership Position: Economic Growth Intern Location: Washington, DC Internship Type: Paid Work Schedule: Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays Hours Per Week: 25–29 Compensation: $20 per hour Start Date: End of August/Early September 2026 Visa Sponsorship: Not available Work Authorization: Applicants must already be eligible to work in the United States. Application Process Interested candidates should: Review the Greater Washington Partnership s mission and recent initiatives. Explore the organization s LinkedIn page and media coverage to understand its work. Prepare an updated resume highlighting relevant education, research, leadership, internship, and communication experience. Submit their application through the organization s official application portal. Application Deadline No application deadline has been specified in the opportunity announcement. Interested applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since internship positions may close once filled. Conclusion The Greater Washington Partnership Economic Growth Internship represents an outstanding opportunity for students and recent graduates seeking practical experience in regional economic development, entrepreneurship, policy research, and cross-sector collaboration. Beyond earning competitive hourly compensation, interns will gain valuable exposure to high-level strategic initiatives that shape one of America s most economically significant regions. Through hands-on involvement in research, stakeholder engagement, innovation programming, and policy implementation, participants will build skills and professional networks that can serve as a strong foundation for future careers in public policy, nonprofit leadership, consulting, business strategy, and economic development. Applicants who are passionate about creating lasting economic impact and contributing to inclusive regional growth should strongly consider applying as soon as possible. title: CGD Research Analyst Job 2026 in London: £46,725–£51,187 Global Development Research Role
summary: The Center for Global Development is recruiting a Research Analyst in London to support its work with the Smart Buys Alliance, an international collaboration focused on identifying and promoting highly cost-effective development interventions. This full-time, mid-level position combines empirical research, quantitative analysis, policy writing, project coordination and event support. The successful candidate will help examine how bilateral donors, development agencies and governments use evidence on cost-effectiveness when making funding and policy decisions. The Research Analyst will be based in London and is expected to work from CGD’s office at least three days each week. The position offers an annual salary of £46,725–£51,187 , together with additional benefits. The role is expected to begin as soon as possible and will initially continue until 29 February 2028 . An extension may be possible, depending on the availability of funding. Applications close on 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM British Summer Time . CGD Research Analyst Job 2026 Overview Key details of the opportunity include: Position: Research Analyst Organisation: Center for Global Development Project: Smart Buys Alliance Location: London, United Kingdom Employment type: Full-time Career level: Mid-level Salary: £46,725–£51,187 per year, plus benefits Start date: As soon as possible Contract duration: Fixed term until 29 February 2028 Extension: Subject to funding availability Posting date: 23 July 2026 Application deadline: 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM BST Office requirement: At least three days per week Work-authorisation requirement: Right to live and work in the United Kingdom About the Center for Global Development The Center for Global Development, commonly known as CGD, is an independent, non-partisan and nonprofit policy research organisation with offices in Washington, DC, and London. CGD conducts empirical research on policies, institutions and financial decisions that affect low- and middle-income countries. Its work examines how governments, international organisations, corporations, development agencies and financial institutions can contribute to more inclusive and sustainable development. The organisation combines research with engagement across the global policy community. Rather than producing analysis solely for academic audiences, CGD seeks to translate research findings into practical recommendations that can influence development policy, financing and implementation. Its work often sits at the intersection of: Development economics Public policy International finance Aid effectiveness Global institutions Poverty reduction Evidence-based decision-making Development cooperation The Research Analyst will support this wider mission by contributing to work on how development organisations identify, assess and use evidence about cost-effective interventions. About the Smart Buys Alliance The Smart Buys Alliance connects development agencies, philanthropic organisations and research institutions seeking to increase investment in effective development interventions. The alliance promotes the use of evidence when governments and donors decide how to allocate limited development resources. Its work is particularly concerned with identifying interventions that can produce substantial positive outcomes relative to their costs. The alliance operates through three principal areas of work. Developing On-Demand Smart Buy Lists The Smart Buys Alliance supports the development of lists identifying development interventions with strong evidence of cost-effectiveness. These resources are intended to help funders and policymakers compare options and direct resources toward programmes that are likely to deliver significant results. Supporting Implementation and Evidence Building Identifying an effective intervention is only one part of the process. The alliance also supports implementation and encourages donors to coordinate their efforts to strengthen the evidence base. This may involve examining how interventions perform in different settings, identifying implementation constraints and understanding whether the results of one programme can be reproduced elsewhere. Convening a Community of Practice The alliance brings together policymakers, researchers, funders and development practitioners to exchange evidence, experience and practical lessons. The Smart Buys Alliance is a collaboration involving: Center for Effective Global Action Cooperation Globale Center for Global Development Global Poverty Research Lab Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab Participating donor agencies and partners The Research Analyst will support CGD’s contribution to this partnership. Purpose of the Research Analyst Position The Research Analyst will provide analytical, operational and administrative support to CGD’s Smart Buys Alliance work. The role is intended to help the project deliver accurate, timely and policy-relevant research outputs. It is not limited to data analysis: the selected candidate will also contribute to writing, coordination, stakeholder engagement and the organisation of policy events. The Research Analyst will report to Michelle Rao, Fellow at CGD Europe , and work closely with members of the broader research team. The role requires someone who can move comfortably between detailed analytical work and practical project coordination. On one day, the Analyst may be cleaning a dataset or reviewing causal-inference evidence; on another, they may be revising a policy report, coordinating a roundtable or arranging travel for project partners. Research and Analytical Responsibilities Analysing Donor Use of Cost-Effectiveness Evidence A major component of the role will involve examining how donor agencies engage with and use evidence about cost-effective development interventions. The Research Analyst may help investigate questions such as: How do donor agencies define cost-effectiveness? What evidence do they use when selecting interventions? How consistently is evidence incorporated into funding decisions? What organisational factors encourage or prevent evidence use? How can the use of cost-effectiveness evidence be monitored? How might donor practices change over time? Work in this area may include: Literature reviews Data collection Data extraction Dataset construction Data cleaning Quantitative analysis Textual analysis Review of policy and organisational documents Textual Analysis Using Large Language Models The position may involve using large language models to support the analysis of textual data. This could include examining development strategies, policy documents, donor reports or other materials to identify patterns in how organisations discuss and apply evidence. Candidates with prior experience using large language models for evidence synthesis or textual analysis will have an advantage. However, this experience is identified as beneficial rather than mandatory. Applicants should understand that the role requires analytical judgement. Tools may assist with large volumes of text, but conclusions must still be transparent, credible and suitable for policy research. Research on Evidence Use in Development Policy The Research Analyst will support wider research on how evidence informs international development policy. This may include: Original data analysis Quantitative research Cost-effectiveness analysis Heterogeneity analysis Causal-inference methods Evidence synthesis Interpretation of empirical findings Preparation of charts and visualisations Heterogeneity analysis may be used to examine whether an intervention produces different effects across populations, countries or implementation settings. Cost-effectiveness analysis may involve comparing the costs and outcomes of different interventions to assess which approaches offer greater value. Drafting Research Outputs The Research Analyst will contribute to drafting and revising: Academic or policy papers Research reports Policy briefs Blogs Monitoring products Analytical summaries Supporting materials for stakeholders The selected candidate must be able to communicate technical findings clearly without flattening the nuance out of them. Policy audiences generally need clarity, not a statistical fog bank. The Analyst will work under the guidance of the Research Fellow and in collaboration with the wider research team. Monitoring Evidence-Use Initiatives The role also involves tracking initiatives intended to increase the use of evidence by: Development organisations Bilateral agencies Governments Donor institutions Research organisations This may require maintaining structured records, following institutional developments and synthesising information from multiple organisations or processes. Convenings and Policy-Engagement Responsibilities Research is only useful when it reaches the people making decisions. The Research Analyst will therefore contribute to workshops, roundtables and other policy-engagement activities. Planning Events The successful candidate will support the planning and organisation of: Workshops Roundtable discussions Research launches Partner meetings Policy events Stakeholder consultations Responsibilities may include preparing timelines, maintaining participant lists, coordinating invitations and ensuring that logistical arrangements are completed. Meeting Coordination The role requires coordinating meetings among participants based in different countries and time zones. The Research Analyst may need to: Identify suitable time-zone options Liaise with participants Manage calendars Confirm attendance Circulate meeting materials Maintain schedules Follow up on agreed actions Strong attention to detail is important because international coordination has a peculiar ability to turn one missing calendar invitation into a minor diplomatic incident. Travel Arrangements The Research Analyst will support travel planning for partners and participants attending Smart Buys Alliance events. This may include coordinating itineraries, gathering traveller information and communicating logistical arrangements. Required Academic Qualifications Applicants must hold a master’s degree in one of the following areas: Economics Public policy International development Development economics A closely related discipline The position requires advanced analytical training, particularly because the successful candidate will work with empirical research, quantitative methods and policy evidence. Required Professional Experience Candidates must have at least four years of professional experience in economic or public-policy analysis related to international development. Relevant experience may have been gained in: Policy research organisations Universities International organisations Government institutions Development agencies Think tanks Consulting organisations NGOs Philanthropic foundations Applicants should demonstrate meaningful responsibility for analytical work rather than only general exposure to development projects. Research and Quantitative Skills Candidates must have strong research and quantitative analytical skills. They should have experience designing and conducting empirical research in an academic or professional environment. Expected capabilities include: Structuring research questions Reviewing relevant literature Working with quantitative datasets Cleaning and validating data Applying appropriate analytical methods Interpreting findings Communicating limitations Producing credible research outputs Knowledge of causal-inference methods is required. This may include familiarity with methods used to estimate the effects of programmes or policies and distinguish causal relationships from simple correlations. Required and Desirable Software Skills Applicants should be able to conduct quantitative analysis and produce visualisations using: R Stata Experience with the following is an advantage: Python Git Large language models Textual-analysis tools Evidence-synthesis methods Candidates should explain how they have used relevant tools in actual research rather than merely listing software names in their CV. Writing and Communication Skills Excellent written communication is required. The successful applicant must be able to summarise complicated empirical findings clearly and concisely for policy audiences. Strong candidates will demonstrate the ability to: Write logically structured research outputs Explain quantitative findings in accessible language Distinguish evidence from interpretation Tailor writing to different audiences Revise work in response to feedback Maintain accuracy while remaining concise Applicants must submit a writing sample, making the quality and relevance of that document particularly important. Organisational and Coordination Experience Candidates should have experience supporting: Committees Working groups Research partnerships Multi-stakeholder processes Cross-institutional initiatives Experience in professional communications, social-media management or event coordination is also relevant. The role requires a person who can manage research responsibilities alongside operational tasks without allowing either side of the job to drift into chaos. Applicants should therefore demonstrate: High attention to detail Ability to manage multiple deadlines Strong calendar and scheduling skills Experience maintaining shared documents Clear and reliable communication Ability to coordinate across institutions Confidence working across time zones Collaboration and Working Style The Research Analyst will work with colleagues and partners from several institutions. CGD is seeking someone with a collaborative and team-oriented working style who can contribute effectively across organisational boundaries. The successful candidate should be able to: Work independently when necessary Seek guidance appropriately Share information with colleagues Respond constructively to feedback Coordinate with external partners Adapt to changing project priorities Maintain professional relationships across institutions Salary and Benefits The annual salary range is: £46,725–£51,187 The appointment also includes excellent benefits, although the vacancy information provided does not list the individual benefit components. The exact salary offered within the range will likely depend on the successful candidate’s experience and qualifications. Contract Duration and Start Date The successful candidate is expected to begin as soon as possible. The position is fixed term and will run until: 29 February 2028 An extension may be possible if additional funding becomes available. Applicants should not assume that an extension is guaranteed. London-Based Hybrid Working Arrangement The position is based in London. The successful candidate must live within commutable distance of CGD’s offices in the SW1 area and attend the office at least three days per week . The position should therefore not be treated as a fully remote opportunity. Applicants should consider the practical implications of commuting to central London before applying. Right-to-Work Requirement Candidates must already have, or be able to obtain, the legal right to live and work in the United Kingdom. The vacancy does not state that visa sponsorship will be provided. Applicants requiring sponsorship should confirm the organisation’s policy before relying on this position as a route to UK work authorisation. Application Requirements Interested candidates must submit: A current CV A cover letter A writing sample Preparing the CV The CV should clearly demonstrate: Relevant academic qualifications At least four years of applicable experience Quantitative research responsibilities Experience with R and Stata Knowledge of causal-inference methods Policy-writing experience Coordination or event-management responsibilities Preparing the Cover Letter The cover letter should explain how the applicant meets the position’s requirements. Candidates should provide specific examples of: Empirical research they have conducted Development-policy questions they have analysed Datasets they have cleaned or managed Quantitative methods they have applied Research they have translated for policy audiences Multi-stakeholder processes they have supported Competing deadlines they have successfully managed Selecting a Writing Sample The writing sample should demonstrate the ability to communicate research clearly. A strong sample may include: A policy brief A research report An analytical blog An academic paper section A development-policy publication Applicants should choose a sample that reflects their own contribution and is relevant to the role. Manual Application Review CGD states that applications will be reviewed manually. No artificial-intelligence system or automated filter will be used to screen applicants. Candidates should still tailor their materials carefully, but they do not need to construct their CV around an imaginary robot guarding the door with a keyword clipboard. Equal Opportunity Statement CGD Europe is an equal-opportunity employer committed to a collaborative, diverse and inclusive workplace. Applicants will be considered without discrimination based on characteristics including: Race Colour Creed National origin Ancestry Gender Gender identity or expression Parental status Veteran status Marital status Disability Religious affiliation Political affiliation Age Sexual orientation Selection will be based on the requirements of the position and the applicant’s qualifications and experience. Application Deadline Applications must be submitted by: 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM BST Candidates should submit before the closing time to avoid last-minute technical problems. International applicants should note that the deadline is stated in British Summer Time. APPLY HERE Conclusion The CGD Research Analyst position offers an experienced international-development researcher the opportunity to contribute to influential work on cost-effectiveness and evidence use in development policy. The role combines quantitative research, policy writing, large-scale textual analysis, coordination and stakeholder engagement. It is especially suited to candidates who can move confidently between data, ideas and the practical machinery of international collaboration. Applicants need a relevant master’s degree, at least four years of professional experience, strong quantitative skills and experience using R and Stata. Knowledge of causal inference is required, while experience with Python, Git, evidence synthesis or large language models would strengthen an application. The position is based in London, offers a salary of £46,725–£51,187 , and will continue until 29 February 2028 , with a possible extension depending on funding. Qualified candidates must submit their CV, cover letter and writing sample by 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM BST . To discover more job opportunities, VISIT HERE . title: Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies 2026–2027: Fully Funded Fellowships, Travel Grants, and Research Opportunities for Early-Career Scholars in the United States and Canada
summary: The Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies 2026–2027 is now accepting applications for its prestigious fellowships and grants designed to strengthen and reshape the future of China studies across North America. Administered by the American Council of Learned Societies (ACLS) and generously supported by the Henry Luce Foundation, the program provides substantial funding, research support, mentorship opportunities, and professional development resources for graduate students, early-career scholars, and researchers working in China studies. As the academic landscape surrounding China continues to evolve, scholars increasingly face numerous challenges, including limited access to research materials, shrinking funding opportunities, geopolitical tensions, and barriers to academic collaboration. Recognizing these challenges, ACLS has redesigned the Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies to better support researchers and ensure that China studies remains a vibrant, inclusive, and globally relevant field. The program offers multiple funding opportunities ranging from travel grants to flexible and long-term fellowships, allowing scholars to pursue innovative research while contributing to public understanding of China, its history, cultures, societies, and global influence. About the Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies Since its establishment in 2012, the Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies has played an important role in supporting scholars throughout North America, particularly those in the early stages of their academic careers. Following extensive consultations with researchers, universities, and stakeholders in 2023, ACLS redesigned the program to respond to the changing needs of the discipline. The new structure focuses not only on providing financial assistance but also on building stronger academic networks, expanding access to research resources, encouraging interdisciplinary collaboration, and fostering publicly engaged scholarship. The program seeks to ensure that future generations of scholars have the resources, support systems, and institutional capacity necessary to produce meaningful research that benefits both academia and the broader public. Program Objectives The redesigned Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies is guided by three major goals: 1. Expand the Field of China Studies The program seeks to broaden China studies by: Supporting diverse scholarly voices Encouraging new perspectives on Chinese history, society, and culture Promoting scholarship from researchers with varied educational and professional backgrounds Supporting institutions that have historically had fewer opportunities in the field 2. Build Sustainable Academic Infrastructure The initiative aims to address long-term challenges affecting China studies by: Building stronger scholarly networks Supporting collaboration among researchers Developing lasting academic infrastructure Creating strategies that strengthen the future of the discipline 3. Promote Public Understanding The program encourages research that helps the wider public better understand: China s history Chinese cultures Contemporary Chinese society China s influence on global communities China s impact on international politics, economics, and culture Fellowship and Grant Opportunities Available for 2026–2027 Applicants may apply for several funding opportunities depending on their academic stage and research needs. 1. Luce/ACLS Travel Grants in China Studies These grants support travel related to China studies research. Grant Value Up to $5,000 Duration Travel may take place at any point during a 12-month period. Intended Applicants Graduate students Non-tenure-track researchers These grants are ideal for scholars who need to: Visit archives Conduct field research Access specialized collections Collaborate with other researchers Participate in research-related activities 2. Flexible Early Career Fellowships Designed specifically for scholars with demanding teaching or service responsibilities. Fellowship Benefits $15,000 stipend No leave from employment is required These fellowships allow recipients to: Conduct research Complete writing projects Prepare journal articles Develop books and manuscripts Advance scholarly publications This opportunity is particularly valuable for faculty members whose teaching or institutional duties make long-term research leave difficult. 3. Long-Term Early Career Fellowships These fellowships provide significant support for scholars who need dedicated time for research. Fellowship Duration Four to nine months Fellowship Funding Minimum stipend: $20,000 Maximum stipend: $45,000 Recipients are expected to take full leave from university responsibilities in order to focus exclusively on research and writing leading toward a major scholarly publication. Supported Academic Fields The Luce/ACLS Program supports research in: Humanities Interpretive social sciences Importantly: There are no restrictions regarding research methodology. There are no restrictions regarding historical time periods. Researchers are encouraged to pursue innovative, interdisciplinary, and creative scholarship. Publicly Engaged Scholarship One of the defining features of the Luce/ACLS Program is its commitment to making academic knowledge accessible to wider audiences. Applicants are strongly encouraged to design research projects that: Inform public understanding Increase public engagement with scholarship Make humanistic knowledge more accessible Demonstrate broader societal relevance ACLS believes that scholarly knowledge should serve the public good rather than remain confined within academic institutions. Mentorship and Professional Networking Beyond financial support, fellows gain access to valuable networking opportunities. The program hosts: Mentorship activities Professional networking events Alumni engagement Community-building opportunities A networking and mentorship event will be organized alongside the Association for Asian Studies Annual Conference. Fellows selected for the 2026–2027 cohort will receive additional information in January 2027. Luce/ACLS China Studies Digital Mapping Project An important component of the program is the Luce/ACLS China Studies Digital Mapping Project. This initiative seeks to improve scholarly access to important research materials by providing: A directory of significant Sinophone collections located outside mainland China A common access plan that helps researchers locate collections across participating institutions Best-practice resources for digitizing and preserving print collections The Digital Mapping Project strengthens research infrastructure while improving long-term access to valuable historical and cultural resources. Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion The Luce/ACLS Program recognizes diversity as an essential component of academic excellence. The program actively seeks applicants representing diverse: Academic disciplines Institutional affiliations Educational backgrounds Personal experiences Research topics Historical periods Scholarly methodologies Applications are welcomed without discrimination based on: Race Ethnicity Gender Sexual orientation Religion National origin Disability Age Other personal identities Selection is based solely on academic merit and program eligibility. Benefits of the Luce/ACLS Program Successful applicants will benefit from: Funding of up to $45,000 Research support Travel funding Dedicated writing time Professional mentorship Academic networking opportunities Participation in scholarly communities Access to valuable research resources Increased opportunities for publication Enhanced professional development Interested applicants should click HERE to apply by selecting a favourable term of their choice and learn more. Application Deadline The following competitions share the same application deadline: Luce/ACLS Early Career Fellowships in China Studies – Flexible Luce/ACLS Early Career Fellowships in China Studies – Long-Term Luce/ACLS Travel Grants in China Studies Application Deadline: November 5, 2026 Applicants are encouraged to begin preparing their application materials well before the deadline and carefully review the eligibility requirements for their chosen competition. Contact Information Applicants seeking additional information should review the respective competition pages or contact the program through the ACLS China Studies office. Institutional administrators, including Offices of Sponsored Projects, are also encouraged to consult the general guidance provided by ACLS regarding institutional application procedures. Conclusion The Luce/ACLS Program in China Studies continues to serve as one of North America s most significant funding initiatives for scholars studying China within the humanities and interpretive social sciences. Through its redesigned fellowships, grants, mentorship programs, and digital resource initiatives, ACLS is investing in the future of China studies by empowering researchers, promoting inclusive scholarship, and strengthening the academic infrastructure needed for long-term success. Whether you are a graduate student seeking travel support, an early-career academic balancing teaching responsibilities, or a recent PhD looking for dedicated research time, this program provides valuable financial assistance and professional opportunities to advance your scholarship. Interested applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements and submit their applications before the November 5, 2026 deadline. title: THRIVE Project 2026: Transforming Women’s Economic Empowerment, Climate Resilience, and Inclusive Livelihoods in Nigeria
summary: Women continue to play a vital role in driving economic growth, strengthening families, and building resilient communities. However, many women—particularly those living in underserved communities and women with disabilities—still face significant barriers to accessing finance, markets, productive resources, and leadership opportunities. Addressing these challenges requires targeted interventions that promote gender equality, economic inclusion, and sustainable development. The Transforming Her Resilience, Inclusion and Value in Economies (THRIVE) project is one such initiative designed to empower women economically while transforming the systems that continue to limit their participation. Implemented by the Women Environmental Programme (WEP) as part of the Christian Aid Women Transforming Economies Signature Programme in Nigeria , THRIVE seeks to create lasting change by improving women s access to dignified work, financial opportunities, entrepreneurship support, climate-resilient livelihoods, and decision-making processes. This comprehensive 48-month initiative focuses on strengthening local economic systems so that women can thrive as entrepreneurs, farmers, business owners, and community leaders while promoting inclusive economic development. About the THRIVE Project The Transforming Her Resilience, Inclusion and Value in Economies (THRIVE) project is a four-year development initiative aimed at transforming local economies to become more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable for women. The project recognizes that meaningful economic empowerment goes beyond providing financial support. It also requires changing the structures, relationships, policies, and social norms that prevent women from fully participating in economic activities. Through collaboration with community stakeholders, financial institutions, women s organizations, policymakers, and development partners, THRIVE seeks to build economic systems that value women s contributions and ensure equal access to opportunities. The project is funded by Christian Aid and implemented by the Women Environmental Programme (WEP) in Nigeria. Project Duration The THRIVE project will run for: 48 months (4 years) This extended implementation period allows for sustainable interventions, long-term capacity building, and measurable improvements in women s economic participation and resilience. Geographic Focus The THRIVE project is currently being implemented in: Nasarawa Eggon Local Government Area (LGA) Nasarawa State Nigeria Communities participating in the project are carefully selected through detailed assessments that consider: Gender inclusion Disability inclusion Market accessibility Community needs Economic vulnerability This approach ensures that resources reach women and communities with the greatest need. The Challenges THRIVE Seeks to Address Across many communities, women continue to face structural inequalities that prevent them from achieving economic independence. THRIVE aims to address several key challenges, including: Limited Access to Finance Many women entrepreneurs and farmers struggle to obtain: Business financing Agricultural loans Investment capital Savings opportunities Financial services Without adequate financial support, expanding businesses or increasing productivity becomes extremely difficult. Limited Access to Productive Assets Women often have fewer opportunities to access essential productive resources such as: Agricultural land Modern farming tools Equipment Technology Business infrastructure These limitations reduce income generation and long-term economic growth. Unsafe and Unequal Market Conditions Many women operate within markets that present significant barriers, including: Gender discrimination Limited market access Low bargaining power Poor infrastructure Unfair trading conditions THRIVE seeks to improve women s ability to participate in profitable and inclusive markets. Unpaid Care Responsibilities Women frequently shoulder unpaid domestic and caregiving responsibilities that reduce the time available for: Business development Skills training Employment Leadership Economic participation Reducing this burden is essential for achieving gender-equitable economies. Limited Participation in Decision-Making Women often have little influence over: Local economic policies Community planning Market governance Resource allocation Development priorities THRIVE supports women s participation in leadership and policy discussions that directly affect their livelihoods. Project Goal The primary goal of THRIVE is to build gender-just economies where women enjoy: Greater economic rights Increased income security Improved access to productive opportunities Equal participation in markets Stronger influence over economic policies Sustainable and resilient livelihoods Ultimately, the project seeks to transform local economic systems into environments where women can succeed without discrimination or structural barriers. APPLY HERE THRIVE s Four Strategic Pillars The project is built around four integrated intervention areas that work together to strengthen women s economic empowerment. 1. Evidence for Change THRIVE generates research and evidence on barriers affecting women to promote informed policy development. Activities include: Research on unpaid care work Studies on disability inclusion Gender analysis Policy advocacy Community consultations Evidence-based recommendations The information gathered helps shape more inclusive economic policies and practices. 2. Enterprise Development and Skills Building The project equips women with practical knowledge and business skills needed for long-term success. Support includes: MSME coaching Entrepreneurship development Business management training Digital literacy training Enterprise growth support Skills development for young women Capacity building for women with disabilities These interventions help women establish, strengthen, and expand their businesses. 3. Financial Inclusion and Market Access Access to finance and profitable markets is critical for sustainable economic growth. THRIVE strengthens women s financial opportunities by: Supporting Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) Connecting women with financial institutions Improving access to capital Facilitating market linkages Expanding business networks Strengthening value chains These efforts enable women to grow sustainable enterprises and increase household incomes. 4. Climate Resilience Climate change continues to threaten livelihoods, particularly for women working in agriculture. title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027 for Early Career Researchers (Fully Funded to Germany)
summary: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and the British Academy have officially opened applications for the Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027 , a prestigious international research collaboration programme designed for early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences . The symposium offers an exceptional opportunity for emerging scholars from the United Kingdom and Germany to collaborate on pressing global issues surrounding the relationship between humans and nature while building long-term international research partnerships. The symposium, scheduled to take place from 21–23 April 2027 , will bring together approximately 30 outstanding early career researchers , with around 15 participants from the United Kingdom and 15 from Germany , creating an interdisciplinary platform for networking, intellectual exchange, and collaborative research. In addition to fully covering participants travel-related expenses, the programme also provides opportunities to compete for seed funding to support future international collaborative research projects. If you are an early career researcher passionate about sustainability, resilience, environmental justice, policy development, or the intersection between society and nature, this symposium presents an outstanding opportunity to connect with leading researchers and develop meaningful international collaborations. About the Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027 The Knowledge Frontiers Symposium is a collaborative initiative jointly organized by the British Academy and the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation . The programme is specifically designed to strengthen research partnerships between scholars in the United Kingdom and Germany while encouraging interdisciplinary approaches to solving today s most complex societal and environmental challenges. The 2027 symposium will be held between: Wednesday, 21 April 2027 Friday, 23 April 2027 Before the physical symposium begins, participants will also have opportunities to engage virtually by discussing research interests, exchanging ideas, and beginning collaborative conversations that can continue during and after the event. Rather than functioning as a traditional academic conference, the symposium emphasizes interactive discussions, collaborative learning, networking, and the development of future joint research initiatives. Symposium Theme Humans and Nature: More Resilient Towards the Future The 2027 edition focuses on the broad interdisciplinary theme: Humans and Nature: More Resilient Towards the Future. The organizers recognize that the relationship between humans and the natural environment has become one of the defining issues of the modern world. Throughout history, there have been different perspectives regarding humanity s place within nature. Some viewpoints argue that humans possess the authority to manage and control nature, while others believe humans are an integral part of nature and should coexist with natural systems in more sustainable and balanced ways. Today, increasing global crises—including climate change, biodiversity loss, technological transformation, economic pressures, environmental degradation, and population growth—have intensified the urgency of reconsidering this relationship. The symposium aims to encourage participants to rethink how societies interact with ecological systems while identifying practical and innovative pathways toward greater resilience. Research Topics Participants are encouraged to explore a wide variety of interdisciplinary perspectives. Potential discussion areas include, but are not limited to: Contested understandings of society and nature Human-nature conceptualizations Environmental and social justice Sustainability challenges Ecological resilience Coupled human-natural systems Ethics and philosophy Political dimensions of environmental governance Economic approaches to sustainability Geographical perspectives Public policy development Knowledge production Narrative development Artistic perspectives on environmental challenges Interdisciplinary research approaches Future resilience strategies Researchers from diverse academic backgrounds are encouraged to contribute fresh perspectives and innovative ideas. Objectives of the Symposium The symposium has several important goals, including: Strengthening collaboration between UK and German researchers. Building long-term interdisciplinary research networks. Encouraging innovative thinking across humanities and social sciences. Promoting international academic partnerships. Supporting future collaborative research initiatives. Developing practical policy solutions for sustainability and resilience. Encouraging knowledge sharing among early career scholars. Providing networking opportunities with leading researchers. Facilitating cross-disciplinary discussions on global challenges. Symposium Format Unlike conventional academic meetings, the Knowledge Frontiers Symposium prioritizes interaction and collaboration. Participants can expect: Interactive research discussions Thematic sessions Collaborative workshops Networking activities Group debates Research idea exchanges Collaborative planning sessions Opportunities to establish future partnerships The programme allocates substantial time for participants to build professional relationships and explore opportunities for future joint projects. Benefits of the Programme Successful applicants will enjoy numerous benefits, including: Fully Funded Participation The symposium covers: Travel costs Accommodation Visa expenses Participants are therefore able to focus entirely on the academic programme without worrying about major travel-related costs. International Networking Participants will have the opportunity to: Meet leading early career researchers. Build long-lasting professional relationships. Expand international academic networks. Identify future collaborators. Research Collaboration Researchers will: Share ongoing research. Exchange innovative ideas. Learn from scholars in different disciplines. Develop interdisciplinary collaborations. Career Development The symposium supports career progression by helping participants: Increase international research visibility. Strengthen collaborative research experience. Build competitive research portfolios. Access future funding opportunities. Opportunity to Secure Seed Funding Participants may receive funding to continue collaborative research after the symposium through competitive seed funding proposals. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy the following eligibility criteria: Be an early career researcher . Be affiliated with a research institution in either the United Kingdom or Germany . Demonstrate strong research interest in the symposium theme. Show commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration. title: AIXI Labs Research Fellowship 2026: Fully Remote AI Safety Fellowship with Monthly Stipend of £2,000–£3,500 (Worldwide Applications Open)
summary: Artificial Intelligence is rapidly transforming industries, economies, and societies around the world. As AI systems become increasingly capable, ensuring they remain safe, reliable, and aligned with human values has become one of the most important scientific challenges of our time. To address these pressing concerns, AIXI Labs is inviting applications for its Research Fellowship , a prestigious opportunity designed for talented researchers interested in advancing the field of AI safety through rigorous theoretical and empirical research. The AIXI Labs Research Fellowship offers participants the opportunity to work alongside some of the world s leading AI safety researchers while receiving a monthly stipend ranging from £2,000 to £3,500 , a dedicated machine learning compute budget, close mentorship, and the flexibility to work fully remotely from anywhere in the world or from the organization s headquarters in London, United Kingdom . Applications are accepted on a rolling basis , making this an excellent opportunity for aspiring AI researchers to join an internationally recognized research community focused on reducing existential risks from advanced artificial intelligence. About AIXI Labs AIXI Labs is a London-based nonprofit research organization dedicated to advancing AI safety through the lens of Algorithmic Information Theory (AIT) . Unlike many organizations that either focus exclusively on abstract mathematical models or highly practical machine learning systems that are difficult to analyze theoretically, AIXI Labs occupies a unique position by combining both rigorous theory and practical applications. The organization s research focuses on developing methods that are: General enough to describe highly capable intelligent agents Mathematically rigorous enough to produce provable safety guarantees Applicable to modern Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI agents The research agenda is built around AIXI , a well-known theoretical model of unbounded artificial superintelligence developed to study idealized intelligent agents. Researchers at AIXI Labs aim to translate theoretical breakthroughs into practical safety techniques applicable to modern AI systems. About the AIXI Labs Research Fellowship The AIXI Labs Research Fellowship is a quarterly rolling fellowship program created for researchers who want to make meaningful contributions to AI safety research. Participants spend approximately one academic quarter working on a focused research project under the guidance of experienced mentors while collaborating with a growing international AI safety community. The fellowship is designed to support independent researchers who wish to explore foundational questions while maintaining enough flexibility to pursue topics aligned with their own expertise and interests. Fellowship Highlights Selected fellows will receive: Monthly stipend between £2,000 and £3,500 Dedicated machine learning compute budget Close mentorship from leading AI researchers Flexible remote work from anywhere in the world Optional opportunity to work from London headquarters Opportunity to publish research papers and technical articles Access to one of the world s emerging AI safety research communities Potential renewal for exceptional fellows Fellowship Duration The fellowship runs on a quarterly basis , with each fellowship lasting approximately one academic quarter . Applications are reviewed continuously throughout the year under a rolling admissions process. Exceptional participants may be invited to extend or renew their fellowship. Fellowship Location Applicants may choose either of the following work arrangements: Fully Remote (Worldwide) London, United Kingdom Researchers can participate from any country while collaborating virtually with mentors and fellow researchers. Financial Support Successful fellows receive substantial financial support throughout the program. This includes: Monthly stipend between £2,000 and £3,500 Dedicated compute budget for AI and machine learning experiments The compute budget enables fellows to perform computationally intensive machine learning research without bearing personal infrastructure costs. Research Mentorship One of the strongest aspects of the fellowship is direct mentorship from AIXI Labs core research leadership. Fellows work closely with: Cole Wyeth — Founder Executive Director Marcus Hutter — Research Director Aram Ebtekar — Founding Research Scientist This close supervision provides participants with valuable guidance while allowing them to maintain ownership over their research projects. Research Focus Areas The fellowship supports projects across a broad range of AI safety topics grounded in algorithmic information theory. Potential research directions include: 1. AI Safety Theory Developing mathematical foundations for understanding safe intelligent agents. 2. Algorithmic Information Theory Applying information-theoretic approaches to model intelligence and alignment. 3. Reinforcement Learning Exploring safer reinforcement learning systems and decision-making agents. 4. Large Language Models Studying the safety, behavior, and alignment of LLM-based agents. 5. AI Alignment Investigating methods for aligning advanced AI systems with human goals. 6. Empirical AI Safety Testing theoretical ideas using practical machine learning experiments. Responsibilities of Fellows Participants are expected to pursue a self-directed research agenda aligned with AIXI Labs mission. Primary responsibilities include: Conduct original AI safety research Design and execute independent research projects Align research with algorithmic-information-theoretic approaches Perform empirical experiments where applicable Produce high-quality written research outputs Publish papers, technical reports, or blog posts Communicate findings to the AI safety and machine learning communities Researchers are encouraged to tailor their projects according to their own strengths and academic interests. Minimum Eligibility Requirements Applicants should demonstrate strong academic preparation in quantitative disciplines. Minimum qualifications include: Research background equivalent to a current PhD student Alternatively, applicants with master s-level mathematical expertise combined with substantial industry or applied research experience may also qualify for primarily empirical projects Strong knowledge of: Probability Statistics Information Theory Reinforcement Learning Excellent written and verbal communication skills Strong interest in reducing existential risks associated with advanced AI Enthusiasm for AI safety research Importantly, prior experience with AIXI or Algorithmic Information Theory is not required . Preferred Qualifications While not mandatory, competitive applicants may possess one or more of the following: Publications at leading AI conferences such as: NeurIPS ICML ICLR ALT COLT Background in: Algorithmic Information Theory Computability Theory Learning Theory Theoretical Computer Science Experience: Fine-tuning Large Language Models Evaluating LLMs Red-teaming AI systems Reinforcement Learning agents Previous involvement with: UAI community AIXI community Related reading groups AIXI Labs emphasizes the quality and impact of an applicant s strongest research contributions over the sheer number of publications.
